title: Bekhorot 16
description: The end of the baraita on disqualified consecrated animals: their offspring, Rav Huna’s chamber, the substitute that must die and the verse “impure to you”; then a new mishna on a flock taken from a gentile as a guaranteed investment, and how many generations of its offspring are exempt from the firstborn.
topics: 🥛 “The principle of the matter” adds the milk of redeemed consecrated animals
🔁 Offspring dedicated to the same offering and redeemed when blemished: a refutation of Rav Huna?
👁️ Rav Huna reads “liable” for slaughter outside: a blemish on the cornea, and Rabbi Akiva’s “if they ascended”
💀 The substitute made after redemption must die: Rav Naḥman, Rav Amram’s challenge and Abaye’s “it bears its mother’s name”
📜 “It is impure to you”: the five sin offerings that die, the substitute of a guilt offering and the negative mitzva
🐑 Tzon barzel from a gentile: why the offspring are exempt, and why it is interest between two Jews
✋ Abaye and Rava: who bears the loss, and “the hand of a gentile is in the middle”
🔢 Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda: how many generations are exempt, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel’s ten

a2.he: אָמַר מָר: אֵין נִפְדִּין תְּמִימִין, וְאֵין מַתְפִּיסָן לְכׇל זֶבַח שֶׁיִּרְצֶה. תְּמִימִים הוּא דְּלָא מִיפַּרְקִי, הָא בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין — מִיפַּרְקִי. לְכׇל שֶׁיִּרְצֶה הוּא דְּאֵין מַתְפִּיסָן, הָא לְאוֹתוֹ זֶבַח — מַתְפִּיסָן.

a3.he: הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ? דְּמַתְפִּיסָן לְאוֹתוֹ זֶבַח, וְנִפְדִּין בְּמוּמָן. נֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַב הוּנָא?

a4.he: אָמַר לְךָ רַב הוּנָא: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין אֵין נִפְדִּין, וְאַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא רֵישָׁא ״נִפְדִּין תְּמִימִים״ — תְּנָא נָמֵי סֵיפָא ״אֵין נִפְדִּין תְּמִימִים״, וְאַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא רֵישָׁא ״לְכׇל זֶבַח שֶׁיִּרְצֶה״ — תְּנָא נָמֵי סֵיפָא ״לְכׇל זֶבַח שֶׁיִּרְצֶה״.

a5.he: וְהַשּׁוֹחֲטָן בַּחוּץ פָּטוּר. רַב הוּנָא מַתְנֵי חַיָּיב, וּמוֹקֵים לַהּ בְּדוּקִין שֶׁבְּעַיִן, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּאָמַר: אִם עָלוּ לֹא יֵרְדוּ.

a6.he: בֵּין לִפְנֵי פִּדְיוֹנוֹ בֵּין לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנוֹ עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה. אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: וּתְמוּרָתוֹ לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנוֹ מֵתָה. מַאי טַעְמָא? הֵיכִי לֶיעְבֵּיד? לַיקְרְבַיהּ — מִכֹּחַ קְדוּשָּׁה דְּחוּיָה קָאָתְיָא, לִיפְרְקַהּ — לָא אַלִּימָא לְמִיתְפַּס פִּדְיוֹנָהּ, הִלְכָּךְ מֵתָה.

a7.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב עַמְרָם: וְתִיתְּכִיל בְּמוּמָהּ לַבְּעָלִים! וְכִי מָה בֵּין זוֹ לִתְמוּרַת בְּכוֹר וּמַעֲשֵׂר? דִּתְנַן: תְּמוּרַת בְּכוֹר וּמַעֲשֵׂר, הֵן וּוְלָדָן וּוְלַד וְלָדָן עַד סוֹף כׇּל הָעוֹלָם — הֲרֵי הֵן כִּבְכוֹר וּמַעֲשֵׂר, וְיֵאָכְלוּ בְּמוּמָן לַבְּעָלִים!

a8.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: זֶה שֵׁם אִמּוֹ עָלָיו וְזֶה שֵׁם אִמּוֹ עָלָיו, זֶה כּוּלּוֹ תְּמוּרַת בְּכוֹר וּמַעֲשֵׂר מִיקַּרְיָא, מָה בְּכוֹר וּמַעֲשֵׂר בְּמוּמָן מִיתְאַכְלָן לַבְּעָלִים, אַף תְּמוּרָתָן מִיתְאַכְלָא.

a9.he: וְזֶה שֵׁם אִמּוֹ עָלָיו, תְּמוּרַת קָדָשִׁים מִיקַּרְיָא, מָה קָדָשִׁים לָא מִיתַּכְלִי אֶלָּא בְּפִדְיוֹן — אַף תְּמוּרָתָן נָמֵי לָא מִיתַּכְלִי אֶלָּא בְּפִדְיוֹן, וְהָא לָא אַלִּימָא לְמִיתְפַּס פִּדְיוֹנַהּ.

a10.he: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן: מִנַּיִן לִתְמוּרַת פְּסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין שֶׁמֵּתָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״מִמַּעֲלֵי הַגֵּרָה... טָמֵא״, הַאי מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְחָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת מֵתוֹת! הָהוּא מִ״מַּפְרִיסֵי הַפַּרְסָה טָמֵא״ נָפְקָא.

a11.he: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: מִנַּיִן לְחָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת מֵתוֹת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״מִמַּפְרִיסֵי הַפַּרְסָה... טָמֵא״. חָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת מֵתוֹת, הִילְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ, אֶלָּא כִּי אֲתָא קְרָא לִתְמוּרַת אָשָׁם.

a12.he: תְּמוּרַת אָשָׁם נָמֵי הִילְכְתָא הִיא, כֹּל שֶׁבַּחַטָּאת מֵתָה — בָּאָשָׁם רוֹעֶה!

a13.he: אֶלָּא, לְעוֹלָם חָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת מֵתוֹת, וְאִצְטְרִיךְ קְרָא וְאִצְטְרִיךְ הִילְכְתָא, דְּאִי מִקְּרָא הֲוָה אָמֵינָא לִרְעִיָּיה, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן הִילְכְתָא לְמִיתָה. וְאִי מֵהִילְכְתָא הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: הֵיכָא דַּעֲבַד אִיקְּרִי וַאֲכַל מֵהָנֵי חָמֵשׁ חַטָּאוֹת — אִיסּוּרָא אִיכָּא, לָאו לֵיכָּא, קָמַשְׁמַע לַן דְּאִיכָּא לָאו.

a14.he: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְאַקּוֹשֵׁי דָּבָר הַבָּא מִמַּעֲלֵי גֵּרָה לְדָבָר הַבָּא ״מִמַּפְרִיסֵי הַפַּרְסָה״, מָה לְהַלָּן בְּמִיתָה — אַף כָּאן בְּמִיתָה.

b1.he: וַלְדוֹתֵיהֶן פְּטוּרִין, וַלְדֵי וַלְדוֹתֵיהֶן חַיָּיבִין. הֶעֱמִיד וַלְדוֹתֵיהֶן תַּחַת אִמּוֹתֵיהֶן — וַלְדֵי וְלָדוֹת פְּטוּרִין, וּוַלְדֵי וַולְדֵי וְולָדוֹת חַיָּיבִים. רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ עַד עֲשָׂרָה פְּטוּרִים, שֶׁאַחְרָיוּתָן לַנׇּכְרִי.

b2.he: רָחֵל שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין עֵז, וְעֵז שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין רָחֵל — פְּטוּרָה מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה, וְאִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין — חַיָּיב.

b3.he: גְּמָ׳ לְמֵימְרָא, דְּכֵיוָן דְּלָא נָקֵט מָרָא זוּזֵי — בִּרְשׁוּתָא דְּמָרָא קָיְימָא?

b4.he: וּרְמִינְהוּ: אֵין מְקַבְּלִין צֹאן בַּרְזֶל מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא רִבִּית, אַלְמָא בִּרְשׁוּתָא דִּמְקַבֵּל קָיְימָא!

b5.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דְּקַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ אוּנְסָא וְזוֹלָא, וְהָא דְּלָא קַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ אוּנְסָא וְזוֹלָא.

b6.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: דְּקַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ אוּנְסָא וְזוֹלָא, ״צֹאן בַּרְזֶל״ קָרֵית לֵיהּ? וְעוֹד, מַאי פַּסְקָא?

b7.he: וְעוֹד, אַדְּתָנֵי סֵיפָא אֲבָל מְקַבְּלִין צֹאן בַּרְזֶל מִן הַגּוֹי — לִיפְלוֹג וְלִיתְנֵי בְּדִידַהּ: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים? דְּלָא קַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ אוּנְסָא וְזוֹלָא, אֲבָל קַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ אוּנְסָא וְזוֹלָא — שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי!

b8.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי דְּלָא קַבֵּיל עֲלֵיהּ אוּנְסָא וְזוֹלָא, וְהָכָא גַּבֵּי בְּכוֹרָה הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא, דְּאִילּוּ אָתֵי גּוֹי בָּעֵי זוּזֵי וְלָא יָהֵיב לֵיהּ — תָּפֵיס לַהּ לִבְהֵמָה, וְאִי לָא מַשְׁכַּח לַהּ לִבְהֵמָה — תָּפֵיס וְלָדוֹת דִּידַהּ, וַהֲרֵי יַד גּוֹי בָּאֶמְצַע, וְכֹל יַד גּוֹי בָּאֶמְצַע — פְּטוּרָה מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה.

b9.he: הֶעֱמִיד וַלְדוֹתֵיהֶן תַּחַת אִמּוֹתֵיהֶן — וַלְדֵי וְלָדוֹת פְּטוּרִים. אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: וְלָדוֹת פְּטוּרִין, וַולְדֵי (ולדותיהן) [וְלָדוֹת] חַיָּיבִין. וְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר: וַלְדֵי וְלָדוֹת נָמֵי פְּטוּרִין, וַולְדֵי וַלְדֵי וְלָדוֹת חַיָּיבִין.

b10.he: תְּנַן: הֶעֱמִיד וְלָדוֹת תַּחַת אִמּוֹתֵיהֶן — וַלְדֵי וְלָדוֹת פְּטוּרִין. טַעְמָא דְּהֶעֱמִיד, הָא לֹא הֶעֱמִיד — לָא. תְּיוּבְתָּא דְרַב יְהוּדָה!

b11.he: אָמַר לָךְ רַב יְהוּדָה: הוּא הַדִּין, אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא הֶעֱמִיד, וְהָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: אֲפִילּוּ הֶעֱמִיד נָמֵי.

b12.he: דְּאוֹרְחֵיהּ דְּגוֹי לְמִיתְפַּס בְּנָהּ, וְהָוֵי כְּמִי דְּלֹא הֶעֱמִיד — וַלְדֵי וְלָדוֹת פְּטוּרִין, וַולְדֵי וַלְדֵי וְלָדוֹת חַיָּיבִין.

b13.he: תְּנַן: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ עַד עֲשָׂרָה דּוֹרוֹת פְּטוּרִין, שֶׁאַחְרָיוּתָן לַנׇּכְרִי. בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב יְהוּדָה דְּאָמַר: נָחֵית תַּנָּא קַמָּא לְדָרֵי —

messages.text: Continued from 15b: a baraita set out the laws of consecrated animals that became blemished. The Gemara has noted that “the principle of the matter” in its former clause adds one who slaughters such an animal outside the Temple courtyard, who is exempt, and that the same phrase in its latter clause…
Gemara
…serves to include its milk in the prohibition, i.e., it is prohibited to consume milk of disqualified consecrated animals that were redeemed.

notes.he: דאסור. ולאתויי שוחטו בחוץ דחייב לא אמרינן משום דא"כ איבעי לן למימר בדוקין שבעין ועוד סיפא קתני לקמן השוחטן בחוץ פטור. וכללא דרישא לא אצטריך לאיתויי חלבו דשרי דהשתא ולדן דכגופן דמי דעובר ירך אמו הוא שרי כל שכן חלבו דמיא בעלמא הוא:
notes.en: To include its milk: that it is forbidden. And we do not say [that the phrase comes] to include one who slaughters it outside, that he is liable, because if so we would have had to say [that it speaks of a blemish] on the cornea of the eye; and furthermore, the latter clause below teaches: “One who slaughters them outside is exempt.” And the principle of the former clause was not needed to include its milk as permitted: since even its offspring, which is like its own body, as a fetus is a limb of its mother, is now permitted, all the more so its milk, which is mere liquid.

messages.text: The Gemara analyzes the baraita. The Master said above: With regard to disqualified sacrificial animals whose consecration preceded their blemish, their offspring are sacred and may not be redeemed while they are unblemished, and one may not dedicate them as any offering he desires.

The Gemara infers: It is only unblemished offspring that one may not redeem, which indicates that one may redeem blemished offspring. Likewise, it is only for any offering he desires that he may not dedicate the offspring, but for the same offering as the mother, one may dedicate the offspring.

notes.he: אותם שנתעברו קודם פדיון ונולדו לאחר פדיון וכגון שתפסן לשום זבח דאלימא קדושתייהו למיתפס פדיונן וכשהוא מתפיסן לשם זבח אין מתפיסן לכל זבח שירצה הא לשם אותו זבח מתפיסן. והיכי משכחת לה פירושא הוא כלומר היכי משכחת תירוצא דמילתא דמשמע בעלי מומין נפדין ולשם זבח אחר לא יתפיסם אלא היכי עביד דמתפיסם לשם אותו הזבח ונפדין במומן כשיפול בהן מום:
notes.en: But blemished ones may be redeemed: those that were conceived before the redemption and born after the redemption, where for example he dedicated them for some offering, so that their sanctity is strong enough to transfer to their redemption. And when he dedicates them for an offering, he does not dedicate them as any offering he desires; but for that same offering, he does dedicate them. “How can you find it” is an explanation; that is, how can you find the resolution of the matter, which implies that blemished ones are redeemed and that he may not dedicate them for another offering? Rather, how does he do it? He dedicates them for the sake of that same offering, and they are redeemed in their blemish when a blemish befalls them.

notes.he: אלמא דבני פדייה נינהו ולשם אותו הזבח מתפיסן משמע נמי דבני פדייה נינהו ואפילו תמימין ותיובתא דרב הונא בתרתי דאמר מתין שלא היו יכולין לבוא בשום ענין לידי פדייה:
notes.en: But blemished ones may be redeemed: evidently they are subject to redemption. And “for that same offering he may dedicate them” also implies they are subject to redemption, even unblemished. And that is a double refutation of Rav Huna, who said they die, since they could not come to redemption in any way.

messages.text: How can you find a situation that includes both of these inferences? They apply in a case where one dedicates the unborn offspring as the same offering for which its mother was consecrated, and it may then be redeemed after having developed a blemish.
Shall we say that this is a conclusive refutation of the opinion of Rav Huna, who maintains that the offspring cannot be redeemed and rules that one must leave them to die?

notes.he: דאמר לעיל כונסן לכיפה והן מתים:
notes.en: Shall we say this is a refutation of Rav Huna: who said above [15b] that one gathers them into a chamber and they die.

messages.text: Rav Huna could have said to you: The inferences upon which the refutation is based are false. Just as these unblemished offspring cannot be redeemed, the same is true with regard to blemished animals, as even blemished offspring cannot be redeemed.
messages.quote: a conclusive refutation of the opinion of Rav Huna

messages.text: And since the former clause taught the phrase: They may be redeemed unblemished, the latter clause also taught the phrase: They may not be redeemed unblemished. And since the former clause taught: As any offering he desires, the latter clause also taught: As any offering he desires. According to Rav Huna, no inferences can be made from these rulings of the baraita because they were phrased in this manner for the sake of symmetry between its two sections, rather than to teach a specific halakha.

notes.he: דחידוש הוא דאפילו תמימים נפדים:
notes.en: And since the former clause taught “they may be redeemed unblemished”: for it is a novelty that even unblemished ones are redeemed.

notes.he: איידי דתנא רישא תנא סיפא ולאו דוקא סיפא (לגרודי):
notes.en: Since it taught the former clause, it taught the latter clause, and the latter clause is not precise.

messages.text: It is stated: And one who slaughters them outside the Temple courtyard is exempt from karet.

notes.he: סיפא דברייתא לעיל אקדשים שקדם הקדשן את מומן קאי ואפילו הכי פטור דאין חייבין על שחיטת חוץ אלא על המתקבל בפנים כדתנן בזבחים בפרק פרת חטאת (זבחים דף קיב.) בעלי מומין בין קבועין בין עוברין שהקריבן בחוץ פטור ומפיק טעמא מהאי קרא ואל פתח אהל מועד לא הביאו הא כל שאינו ראוי לבא אל פתח אהל מועד אין חייבין עליו:
notes.en: And one who slaughters them outside is exempt: the latter clause of the baraita above refers to sacrificial animals whose consecration preceded their blemish, and even so he is exempt, since one is liable for slaughter outside only for what is acceptable inside. As we learned in Zevaḥim, in the chapter Parat Ḥatat (Zevaḥim 112a): “Blemished animals, whether with permanent or temporary blemishes, that one offered outside: he is exempt.” And it derives the reason from the verse “and has not brought it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting”: whatever is not fit to come to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, one is not liable for it.

notes.he: והאי השוחטן בחוץ פטר אית ביה תימהא ולא אברייתא קא מהדר ולא אמתניתין דבהא ברייתא לא איירי בה משוחטן בחוץ ואי אמתניתין אהא דאבל אם קדם הקדשן את מומן קאי והשוחטן בחוץ חייב איבעי למימר הילכך (איכא) [ליכא] למיקם אמאי (לא) קא מהדר אבל אמר (לך) [לי] ר' מסתברא דאברייתא קאי אמאי דקאמר כללו דרישא לאתויי שוחטן בחוץ דפטור:
notes.en: And this “one who slaughters them outside is exempt” is puzzling: it does not seem to refer back to the baraita or to the mishna. That baraita did not speak of one who slaughters them outside; and if it refers to the mishna, to the case “but if their consecration preceded their blemish,” it should have said “one who slaughters them outside is liable.” So there is no way to establish what it refers to. But my teacher told me: it is reasonable that it refers to the baraita, to what the Gemara said: the principle of the former clause comes to include one who slaughters them outside, that he is exempt.

messages.text: Rav Huna taught this as: One who slaughters them outside the Temple courtyard is liable to receive karet, and he interprets it as referring to a case involving an animal with a minor blemish, such as on the cornea of the eye. And the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Akiva, who says:

notes.he: כדקתני מתני':
notes.en: Rav Huna teaches “liable”: [in the baraita,] as the mishna [14a] teaches.

notes.he: דמתקבל בפנים הוא:
notes.en: And he establishes it as a blemish on the cornea of the eye: which is accepted inside [if it was brought up].

notes.he: ורב הונא מתני חייב ומוקים להאי בקדם (מום קבוע להקדישן) [הקדשן את מומן] במום בדוקין שבעין דאינו נראה בגלוי כשאר מומין:
notes.en: And Rav Huna teaches “liable,” and establishes this where their consecration preceded their blemish, with a blemish on the cornea of the eye, which is not visible openly like other blemishes.

messages.text: Although animals with a minor blemish may not be sacrificed ab initio, if they ascended the altar they shall not descend and are sacrificed.

notes.he: בשחיטת קדשים בפ' המזבח מקדש (זבחים דף פד.) אם עלו לא ירדו. דוקין טיל"א כגון (ישעיהו מ) הנוטה כדוק שמים. ולהכי לא ירדו דאין מומן ניכר כל כך הכי תנן בזבחים בפ' המזבח מקדש הראוי לו (דף פד.) ר' עקיבא מכשיר בבעלי מומין כלומר דאם עלו לא ירדו ואמר רבי יוחנן בגמ' לא הכשיר רבי עקיבא אלא בדוקין שבעין הואיל וכשירין בעופות והוא שקדם הקדישן את מומן. ל"א דוקין שיש לו מום בעפעפים ולהכי קרי לעפעפים דוק על העין כרקיע דהכי אמרינן בספרי אגודות העין דומה לעולם קטן העפעפים כנגד הרקיע והתחתון כנגד הארץ והלבן שמקיף את העין כנגד ים אוקיינוס שסובב את העולם והשחור שבו שהוא עגול דומה לגלגל חמה:
notes.en: And in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, who says: in [the order of] the slaughter of sacrificial animals, in the chapter HaMizbe’aḥ Mekaddesh (Zevaḥim 84a), “if they ascended they shall not descend.” Dukin: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss), as in “who stretches out the heavens like a film [dok]” (Isaiah 40:22). And they do not descend because their blemish is not so noticeable. So we learned in Zevaḥim, in the chapter HaMizbe’aḥ Mekaddesh (84a): “Rabbi Akiva deems blemished animals fit,” that is, if they ascended they do not descend; and Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the Gemara there: Rabbi Akiva deemed fit only those with a blemish on the cornea of the eye, since such birds are fit, and only where their consecration preceded their blemish. Another explanation: dukin is a blemish on the eyelids, and the eyelids are called dok because they lie over the eye like the firmament. For so we say in the Sifrei: The parts of the eye resemble a small world: the eyelids correspond to the firmament, the lower one to the earth, the white that surrounds the eye to the ocean that encircles the world, and the round black within it resembles the orb of the sun.

notes.he: ואליבא דרבי עקיבא דאמר במסכת זבחים אם עלו לא ירדו וכיון דלגבי מזבח אם עלו לא ירדו כי שחיט להו בחוץ מיחייב:
notes.en: And in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, who says in tractate Zevaḥim: if they ascended they shall not descend. And since, as regards the altar, if they ascended they do not descend, when one slaughters them outside he is liable.

messages.text: Since an animal with a minor blemish is potentially suitable for sacrifice, one who slaughters it outside the Temple courtyard is liable to receive karet.

The Gemara continues analyzing the baraita, which teaches: Whether before its redemption or after its redemption, an animal whose consecration preceded its blemish renders an animal that was a substitute for it sacred.
And its substitute that was imbued with sanctity after its redemption must die.

What is the reason? What are we to do? Shall we sacrifice it? It cannot be sacrificed, as it received its status from the deferred sanctity of the redeemed blemished animal and is therefore unfit for the altar. Shall we redeem it? It cannot be redeemed, as its sanctity is not strong enough to be transferable to the money for its redemption. Therefore, it must die.

notes.he: שכבר נפדו:
notes.en: Deferred sanctity: since they had already been redeemed.

notes.he: ואם תאמר מאי שנא מולדות דאיעבר ואתיליד לאחר פדיונן דחשבינן לעיל ולד צבי ואיל ויש לומר דולדות אין בהן קדושה אלא מכח אמן וכיון שנפדית פקעה קדושתו לגמרי כצבי וכאיל ואע"ג דאיכא איסור גיזה ועבודה אין כח לאיסור מועט כזה שיחול על ידו קדושה על הולדות אבל תמורת קדושה (בההיא) וכיון דגלי קרא שחלה על בעלת מום קבוע חלה ה"ה לאחר פדיונן אלא דלא קרבה אבל תמורה דלפני פדיונן קרבה ועדיפא מולדות דלפני פדיונן דאיכא מ"ד לעיל לרעייה וכן מוכח לשון הקונטרס דבסמוך גבי מנין לתמורת פסולי המוקדשין שמתה ופי' רש"י כגון לאחר פדיונו דלא מצי למיקרב והא דאצטריך קרא דממעלי הגרה בסמוך ללאו אתא דמסברא ידענו דלא קרבה כדאמר רב נחמן הכא וכה"ג אמר בסמוך גבי חמש חטאות ועוד יש לפרש דקרא וסברא צריכי דאי לאו קרא הוה אמינא לא קדשה כלל כצבי ואיל כולדות דאיעבר ואוליד לאחר פדיונן ואי לאו סברא הוה אמינא ירעה וטמא הוא דקרא הוי ימתין עד שיהא טמא ויפול בו מום כדפי' הקונטרס בסמוך והא דפריך רב עמרם ותיתכיל במומה לבעלים אסברא דרב נחמן פריך:
notes.en: In brief: And its substitute after its redemption dies. If you ask: how is this different from offspring conceived and born after their mother’s redemption, which we counted above [15b] like the offspring of a gazelle or a hart [i.e., non-sacred]? Answer: offspring have sanctity only by force of their mother, and once she is redeemed her sanctity lapses entirely, as with a gazelle or a hart; the remaining prohibition of shearing and labor is too minor to make sanctity take effect on the offspring. But the sanctity of a substitute is different: since the verse revealed that it takes effect even on [an animal with] a permanent blemish, it likewise takes effect after redemption, only it is not sacrificed. A substitute made before redemption is sacrificed, and so it is superior to offspring born before redemption, which according to one opinion above are for grazing. So too Rashi’s wording below (“from where is it derived that the substitute of disqualified consecrated animals dies”: “for example after their redemption, since it cannot be sacrificed”). And the verse “of them that chew the cud” is needed below for a negative mitzva, since by reasoning we already knew it is not sacrificed, as Rav Naḥman says here; and it says the same below of the five sin offerings. Alternatively, verse and reasoning are both needed: without the verse I would say the substitute is not sanctified at all, like a gazelle and a hart, like offspring conceived and born after redemption; and without the reasoning I would say it grazes, reading the verse’s “it is impure” as “wait until it becomes impure,” i.e., blemished, as Rashi explains below. And Rav Amram’s objection, “let it be eaten in its blemish by the owners,” is aimed at Rav Naḥman’s reasoning. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: מכח קדושה דחויה קא אתי כיון דלאחר פדיון נעשו תמורה:
notes.en: It comes by force of deferred sanctity: since they were made a substitute after redemption.

messages.text: But let the substitute be eaten in its blemished state by the owners. After all, what is the difference between this substitute and the substitute of a firstborn or of an animal tithe offering, which may be eaten? As we learned in a mishna:
messages.quote: And its substitute after its redemption must die

notes.he: ימתינו עד שיוממו ויאכלו לבעלים כבכור ומעשר שאין נפדין אלא נאכלין במומן. אלמא כיון דלא מצי קרבי כדאמר במס' תמורה (דף ה: ע"ש) אך בכור שור וגו' הן קריבין ואין תמורתן קריבין נאכלין במומן לבעלים הכי נמי ליעבד הכי:
notes.en: And let it be eaten in its blemish: let them wait until it becomes blemished, and let it be eaten by the owners, like a firstborn and a tithe animal, which are not redeemed but are eaten in their blemish. Evidently, since [their substitutes] cannot be sacrificed, as it says in tractate Temura (5b), “Only the firstborn of an ox…”: they are sacrificed, but their substitutes are not sacrificed, and they are eaten in their blemish by the owners. Here too, let it be done so.

messages.text: With regard to the substitute of a firstborn and of an animal tithe offering, both they, the substitutes themselves, and their offspring, and the offspring of their offspring, forever, i.e., for all future generations, are like the firstborn and the animal tithe offering, respectively, and therefore they are eaten in their blemished state by the owners.
Why is the blemished substitute of a firstborn or an animal tithe permitted whereas the substitute of a disqualified consecrated animal remains forbidden?
@Rav Amram This one bears its mother’s name and that one bears its mother’s name, i.e., each substitute is subject to the same halakha as the animal for which it was substituted.
messages.quote: what is the difference between this substitute and the substitute of a firstborn

notes.he: אמו קרי אותו שבא מכחו:
notes.en: Its mother’s name is upon it: he calls “its mother” the animal by whose force it comes [i.e., the animal for which it was substituted].

messages.text: This animal is entirely called a substitute of a firstborn or an animal tithe offering: Just as a firstborn and an animal tithe offering are eaten in their blemished state by the owners, so too, their substitute is eaten even when it is blemished.

notes.dh: מה בכור ומעשר במומן מתאכלין לבעלים
notes.he: דבכור כי לית ביה מום מקריב אימורין דידיה על גבי מזבח ואינו אוכלן כהן וכי איתיליד ביה מומא נאכל כולו לכהן. בהמת מעשר דלית ביה מומא מסיק ליה לירושלים ואכיל ליה ישראל גופיה ומקריב אימורין למזבח:
notes.en: Just as a firstborn and a tithe animal are eaten in their blemish by the owners: for a firstborn without a blemish, its sacrificial portions are offered on the altar, and the priest does not eat them; and when a blemish arises in it, it is eaten entirely by the priest. A tithe animal without a blemish is brought up to Jerusalem and the Israelite himself eats it, and he offers its sacrificial portions on the altar;

notes.he: וכי איתליד ביה מומא נאכל כולו לישראל והאי לבעלים דקתני הכא לאו לחד בעלים קאמר אלא כל חד וחד כדאיתיה האי לבעלים דידיה והאי לבעלים דידיה:
notes.en: and when a blemish arises in it, it is eaten entirely by the Israelite. And “by the owners” taught here does not mean one owner; rather, each as it is: this one by its owners and that one by its owners.

messages.text: And likewise, this substitute for a redeemed animal whose consecration preceded its blemish bears its mother’s name, i.e., it is called the substitute of a sacrificial animal: Just as sacrificial animals are eaten only once they have been rendered permitted through redemption, so too, their substitutes are also eaten only through redemption.
But the sanctity of this particular substitute is not strong enough to be transferable to money for its redemption, and therefore it cannot be redeemed. Consequently, it may not be eaten.

notes.dh: והא בהמה לא אלימא למיתפס פדיונה
notes.he: הילכך מתה:
notes.en: But this animal’s sanctity is not strong enough to transfer to its redemption: therefore it dies.

messages.text: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with the opinion of Rav Naḥman:

From where is it derived with regard to the substitute of a disqualified consecrated animal that it must die? It is derived from a verse, as the verse states: “Nevertheless, these you shall not eat, of them that only chew the cud, or of them that only have a split hoof…it is impure to you.”

verse.he: אַךְ אֶת־זֶה לֹא תֹאכְלוּ מִמַּעֲלֵי הַגֵּרָה וּמִמַּפְרִסֵי הַפַּרְסָה אֶת־הַגָּמָל כִּי־מַעֲלֵה גֵרָה הוּא וּפַרְסָה אֵינֶנּוּ מַפְרִיס טָמֵא הוּא לָכֶם׃
verse.en: The following, however, of those that either chew the cud or have true hoofs, you shall not eat: the camel—although it chews the cud, it has no true hoofs: it is impure for you;

notes.he: כגון דלאחר שנפדו הקדשים התפיסן בתמורה דלא מצו למיקרב:
notes.en: From where is it derived that the substitute of disqualified consecrated animals dies: for example, where after the consecrated animals were redeemed he made a substitute for them, which cannot be sacrificed.

notes.he: דסיפיה דקרא כתיב טמא הוא לכם ודרשינן הכי יש לך דבר שיש בו סימני טהרה ואסור באכילה ואיזו זו תמורת פסולי המוקדשין:
notes.en: Of them that chew the cud … it is impure: for at the end of the verse it is written “it is impure to you,” and we expound it thus: you have something that has the signs of purity and is forbidden to eat. Which is it? The substitute of disqualified consecrated animals.

notes.he: והא דדרשינן בפ"ק (לעיל בכורות דף ו.) יש לך דבר שהוא מעלה גרה ואי אתה אוכלו כגון טהור שנולד מן הטמא התם דריש מרישיה דקרא ואת אלה לא תאכלו והכא דריש מסיפיה דקרא טמא הוא לכם אי נמי תרי קראי כתיבי:
notes.en: The verse states: “Of them that chew the cud.” And as for what we expound in the first chapter (above, 6a), “you have something that chews the cud and yet you do not eat it, such as a kosher animal born of a non-kosher one”: there it expounds the beginning of the verse, “Nevertheless these you shall not eat,” and here it expounds the end of the verse, “it is impure to you.” Alternatively, two verses are written.

notes.he: כלומר יש בהמה שיש לה סימני טהרה והיא אסורה היינו תמורת בעלי מומין לאחר פדיונן:
notes.en: “Of them that chew the cud … impure”: that is, there is an animal that has the signs of purity and is forbidden; that is the substitute of blemished animals after their redemption.

messages.text: The extraneous phrase “impure to you” indicates that there exists an animal which possesses the signs of a kosher animal but is nevertheless prohibited in consumption, and that is the substitute of a disqualified consecrated animal.
But isn’t that extraneous phrase necessary for the halakha of the five sin offerings that are left to die, which may not be eaten?

notes.he: מפרש בתמורה (דף כא:):
notes.en: Five sin offerings: they are explained in Temura (21b).

messages.text: No; that halakha is derived from the phrase: “Of them that only have a split hoof…is impure.”
This is also taught in a baraita:

From where is it derived that there are five sin offerings that are left to die? The verse states: “Of them that have a split hoof…is impure to you,” which indicates that there is a second category of animals that possess the signs of a kosher animal, but that are nevertheless prohibited in consumption.
But isn’t the category of the five sin offerings that are left to die a halakha learned as a tradition, not from a verse?
Rather, when that verse came, it came to teach that the substitute of a guilt offering may not be sacrificed and is left to graze until it develops a blemish.

notes.he: שתהא רועה דאשם לא קרב נדבה הלכך תמורתו לא קרבה והא טמא דקרא ה"ק הניחוהו עד שיהא טמא כלומר שיפול בו מום:
notes.en: For the substitute of a guilt offering: that it grazes. For a guilt offering is not brought as a voluntary offering, so its substitute is not sacrificed. And the verse’s “impure” means: leave it until it becomes “impure,” that is, until a blemish befalls it.

notes.dh: אלא כי אתא קרא לתמורת אשם
notes.he: והכי פירושא דברייתא מנין לחמש חטאות מתות וכנגדן באשם רועה וטמא הוא היינו שירעה עד שיסתאב כדפירש הקונטרס:
notes.en: Rather, when the verse came, it was for the substitute of a guilt offering: and this is the meaning of the baraita: from where is it derived that the five sin offerings die, and that their counterparts in a guilt offering graze? And “it is impure” means that it grazes until it becomes unfit [through a blemish], as Rashi explained.

notes.he: לתמורת אשם הוא דאיצטריך דאינה מתה אלא רועה שיהא אסורה:
notes.en: It was needed for the substitute of a guilt offering, which does not die but grazes, so that it be forbidden.

messages.text: The halakha of a substitute for a guilt offering is also a halakha learned as a tradition, as stated in the principle: In any case where a sin offering is left to die, a guilt offering is left to graze. Since the substitute of a sin offering is left to die, it is established by tradition that the substitute of a guilt offering is left to graze, and therefore no verse is required to teach this halakha.

notes.he: ותמורת חטאת היינו אחת מחמש חטאות מתות:
notes.en: Whatever in a sin offering dies: and the substitute of a sin offering is one of the five sin offerings that die.

notes.he: אומר רבינו תם דרעייה מדרבנן היא ולפי שתקנו חכמים רעייה נקט בכל דוכתא באשם רועה אבל הילכתא הכי איתא מדאורייתא דכל שבחטאת מתה באשם קרב עולה כדאמר בפסחים שילהי (סוף) פרק אלו דברים (פסחים דף עג.) אשם שניתק לרעייה ושחטו כשר לעולה ושם פירשתי לה:
notes.en: Whatever in a sin offering dies, in a guilt offering grazes: Rabbeinu Tam says that the grazing is rabbinic, and because the Sages instituted grazing, it says everywhere “in a guilt offering it grazes.” But the halakha by Torah law is this: whatever in a sin offering dies, in a guilt offering is sacrificed as a burnt offering, as it says in Pesaḥim at the end of the chapter Elu Devarim (Pesaḥim 73a): a guilt offering that was set aside to graze, and he slaughtered it, is fit as a burnt offering. And there I explained it.

messages.text: Rather, the verse is actually the source for a halakha that applies to the five sin offerings left to die. And both a verse is necessary and the halakha learned as a tradition is also necessary to determine the final course of action that one should take.

If the concept of the five sin offerings had been derived from the verse alone, I would say that the five sin offerings are left to graze. Therefore, the halakha learned through tradition teaches us that they are left to die.

And if this ruling were based only on the halakha learned as a tradition, I would say: In a case where one happened to eat from one of these five sin offerings, there is a prohibition that he violated, but not a negative mitzva, for which one is liable to receive lashes. The verse therefore teaches us that there is a negative mitzva here as well.

notes.he: דאין עובר בלאו:
notes.en: There is no negative mitzva: he does not transgress a negative mitzva.

notes.he: לא תאכלו ממעלי הגרה:
notes.en: That there is a negative mitzva: “These you shall not eat, of them that chew the cud.”

notes.he: ואי מהלכתא גרידתא הוה אמינא היכא דעבר ואיקרי ואכל כו' קמ"ל קרא דאיכא לאו דכתיב את זה לא תאכלו. לישנא אחרינא. ומאחר דהלכתא איכא קרא למה ליה למיקם עליה בעשה דכתיב אותה תאכלו ויש לך אחרת שהיא מפרסת פרסה דאית בה לאו אי אקרבה והיינו חמש חטאות ולאו הבא מכלל עשה עשה. והכי מסתברא כלישנא בתרא דהכי נמי גרסינן בתמורה בפרק אלו קדשים וכי איצטריך קרא דאי מקריב ליה קאי עליה בעשה. ואיבעית אימא חמש חטאות לא צריכי קרא אלא לאקושי דבר הבא ממעלי הגרה דהיינו תמורת בעלי מומין לדבר הבא ממפריסי פרסה דהיינו חמש חטאות דנפקי מהתם מה להלן בחמש חטאות מתות אף תמורת בעלי מומין שנפדו נמי והיינו כרב נחמן:
notes.en: And had it been from the halakha alone, I would say that where one happened to eat, etc.; it teaches us that there is a negative mitzva, as it is written “these you shall not eat.” Another version: since there is a halakha, why is the verse needed? To place it under a positive mitzva, as it is written “that you shall eat” [Leviticus 11:3], and you have another animal with a split hoof that is under a “not” if he offered it [the wording here is unclear], namely the five sin offerings; and a negative derived from a positive statement has the force of a positive mitzva. And the latter version is the more reasonable, for so too we read in Temura, in the chapter Elu Kodashim: “And why was the verse needed? So that if he offers it, he stands in violation of a positive mitzva.” And if you wish, say: the five sin offerings do not need a verse; rather, it is to juxtapose an item that comes from “them that chew the cud,” that is, the substitute of blemished animals, with an item that comes from “them that have a split hoof,” that is, the five sin offerings, which are derived from there: just as there the five sin offerings die, so too the substitute of blemished animals that were redeemed. And this is in accordance with Rav Naḥman.

messages.text: And if you wish, say instead that the halakha of the five sin offerings left to die is in fact a halakha learned as a tradition, and therefore no verse is required for its own sake. Rather, the verse: “Of them that have a split hoof,” serves to juxtapose an item that comes, i.e., that is derived, from the mention of animals who chew their cud, referring to the substitutes of disqualified consecrated animals, with an item that comes from animals who have a split hoof, referring to the five sin offerings: Just as there, the sin offerings are left to die, so too here, the substitutes are left to die.

notes.he: להכי אתא ממפריסי הפרסה דמשתעי בחטאות המתות להקיש דבר הבא ממעלי הגרה תמורת פסולי המוקדשין לאחר פדיונן דנפקא ממעלי הגרה לדבר הבא ממפריסי הפרסה חטאות המתות:
notes.en: And if you wish, say: this is why “of them that have a split hoof” comes, which speaks of the sin offerings that die: to juxtapose an item that comes from “them that chew the cud,” namely the substitute of disqualified consecrated animals after their redemption, which is derived from “them that chew the cud,” with an item that comes from “them that have a split hoof,” namely the sin offerings that die.

messages.text: Mishna

With regard to one who receives animals as part of a guaranteed investment from a gentile, i.e., the Jew receives the animals to raise them and commits to pay a fixed price at a later date even if they die or their value decreases, and the offspring born in the interim are divided between the gentile and the Jew,

notes.he: ששם לו עובד כוכבים בהמותיו בדמים קצובין ולתת לו אותן דמים עד עשר שנים בין מתו בין הוזלו ואותן ולדות שיהיו להן עד אותו זמן יהיו ביניהם:
notes.en: MISHNA. One who receives tzon barzel: where a gentile valued his animals for him at fixed prices, [the Jew undertaking] to pay him those prices within up to ten years, whether they died or dropped in value; and the offspring they have until that time will be divided between them.

notes.dh: המקבל צאן ברזל מן העובד כוכבים
notes.he: כלומר דמקבל מיניה בהמה לשעבד עליו שיעבוד קשה כברזל. כגון שקיבל ישראל עליו אם יפחתו דמיה או תמות שישלם לעובד כוכבים כמה ששמין אותה עכשיו ואם תעשה ולדות שיהו בין שניהן הולדות:
notes.en: One who receives tzon barzel from a gentile: that is, he receives an animal from him, binding himself with an obligation as hard as iron [barzel]; for example, the Jew took upon himself that if its value falls or it dies, he will pay the gentile what it is valued at now, and if it bears offspring, the offspring will be between the two of them.

messages.text: their direct offspring are exempt from the mitzva of the firstborn if they give birth to a male, but the offspring of their direct offspring are obligated in the mitzva of the firstborn if they gave birth to a male.

notes.he: מן הבכורה:
notes.en: Their offspring are exempt: from the firstborn.

notes.he: של אותן צאן ברזל כשיגדלו ויבכרו יפטרו מן הבכורה. וטעמא מפרש בגמ' דכיון דאי לא יהיב ליה זוזי לעובד כוכבים תפיס בהמה ואי לא משכח בהמה תפיס ולדות אישתכח דשייכא יד עובד כוכבים באמן:
notes.en: Their offspring: of those tzon barzel animals, when they grow up and give birth for the first time, are exempt from the firstborn. The reason is explained in the Gemara: since if he does not pay the gentile money, he seizes the animal, and if he does not find the animal he seizes the offspring, it turns out that the gentile’s hand is involved in their mother.

notes.he: ולדי ולדות של צאן ברזל המגיעות לחלקו של ישראל כשיהיו להן ולדות בכורות (ינתנו לכהן) דהיינו רביעית לצאן ברזל ינתן לכהן:
notes.en: And the offspring of offspring are obligated: the offspring of the offspring of the tzon barzel that fall to the Jew’s share, when they have offspring, the firstborns [are given to the priest]; that is, the fourth generation of the tzon barzel is given to the priest.

notes.he: של אותו צאן ברזל מה שהן יולדות פטורה מן הבכורה לפי שחצין של עובדי כוכבים. ועוד משום דאמרינן בגמ' דאי לא משכח לה לבהמה תפיס ולדות דילה:
notes.en: And the offspring: what those tzon barzel animals bear is exempt from the firstborn, because half of them belong to the gentile; and also because we say in the Gemara that if he does not find the animal, he seizes its offspring.

notes.he: ולדי של ולדות חייב בבכורה חלק של ישראל דכולי האי ולדי ולדות לא תפיס עובד כוכבים בשבילה:
notes.en: The offspring of offspring: the offspring of the offspring are obligated in the firstborn, in the Jew’s share, for the gentile does not go so far as to seize the offspring of offspring on its account.

messages.text: If the Jew established their offspring in place of their mothers for collection in case the mothers die, the offspring of their direct offspring are exempt and the offspring of the offspring of their direct offspring are obligated.

notes.he: שפתח לו פתח לעובד כוכבים להיות לו כח בולדות ואמר לו אם ימותו הבהמות תטול הולדות המגיעות לחלקי ויהיו תחת ידי באותן דמים עד אותו זמן עצמו:
notes.en: He established offspring in place of their mothers: he opened a door for the gentile to have a claim on the offspring, and said to him: If the animals die, take the offspring that fall to my share, and they will be in my hands for those same sums until that same time.

notes.he: השתא אלימא יד עובד כוכבים ושייכא בדור אחר טפי הלכך ולדות של אותן ולדות שהן ולדי ולדות לצאן הברזל פטורין דשייכא בהו יד עובד כוכבים וכשיהא להם בכור לא ינתן לכהן:
notes.en: And their offspring: now the gentile’s hand is stronger and reaches one more generation; therefore the offspring of those offspring, which are the offspring of the offspring of the tzon barzel, are exempt, since the gentile’s hand reaches them, and when they have a firstborn it is not given to the priest.

notes.he: פירש הקונטרס שפתח לו הפתח להיות לו כח בולדות ואמר לו אם ימותו הבהמות תטול הולדות המגיעות לחלקי ויהא תחת ידי באותן דמים ובפירוש משמע בגמרא כמו שפירשתי לשם אבל בתוספתא קתני מתו האמהות והעמיד הולדות:
notes.en: He established offspring in place of their mothers: Rashi explained that he opened a door for him to have a claim on the offspring, and said to him: If the animals die, take the offspring that fall to my share, and it will be in my hands for those sums. And this is clearly implied in the Gemara, as I explained there [below, on 16b]. But in the Tosefta it teaches: “The mothers died and he established the offspring.”

notes.he: העמידו ולדות תחת אימותיהן שאם תמות הבהמה שיקח העובד כוכבים הולדות תחתיה אותן ולדות הרי הן כצאן [עצמו] שולדותיהן מה שהן יולדת פטורה מן הבכורה. ולדי ולדותיהן חייבין ר' שמעון כו':
notes.en: He established the offspring in place of their mothers: that if the animal dies, the gentile will take the offspring in its place. Those offspring are like the flock [itself], so that what they bear is exempt from the firstborn; the offspring of their offspring are obligated. Rabbi Shimon, etc. [Rabbeinu Gershom’s text reads Rabbi Shimon here.]

messages.text: Even until ten generations, the offspring are exempt, as they all serve as a guarantee for the gentile, because if he does not receive the fixed payment for the animal, he will collect his debt from any offspring born to it or its offspring.

notes.he: דלעולם כל מה דמשכח עובד כוכבים תפיס:
notes.en: Since their liability is to the gentile: for whatever the gentile finds, he always seizes.

messages.text: A ewe that gave birth to a goat of sorts and a goat that gave birth to a ewe of sorts are exempt from the mitzva of the firstborn. And if the offspring has some of the characteristics of its mother, it is obligated in the mitzva of firstborn.
Gemara

The mishna teaches that animals given to a Jew as a guaranteed investment by a gentile are not subject to their offspring being counted a firstborn because they belong to the gentile. Is this to say that since the owner did not yet take the money that will be owed to him, the investment itself stands in the owner’s possession, i.e., the owner is still regarded as such?
messages.quote: their direct offspring are exempt from the mitzva of the firstborn

notes.he: העובד כוכבים זוזי ברשותיה דעובד כוכבים קיימי:
notes.en: GEMARA. Since the gentile did not take the money: they stand in the gentile’s possession.

notes.he: דברשותא דמרה דעובד כוכבים קיימא שמפני כך פטורה מן הבכורה:
notes.en: Is that to say: that it stands in the possession of its owner, the gentile, and that is why it is exempt from the firstborn.

messages.text: And the Gemara raises a contradiction to this conclusion from a mishna:

One may not accept from a Jew sheep to raise or other items to care for as a guaranteed investment, in which the terms of the transaction dictate that the one accepting the item takes upon himself complete responsibility to repay its value in the event of depreciation or loss, but receives only part of the profit. This is because it is a loan, as the principal is fixed and always returned to the owner, and any additional sum the owner receives is interest.

notes.dh: אין מקבלין צאן ברזל מישראל מפני שהוא רבית
notes.he: בפרק איזהו נשך (ב"מ דף ע:) פירש"י רבית ששם אותם עליו במעות וכל זמן שאין נותן מעותיו חולקין השכר ואע"ג דמשנה יתירא היא דהא תנא ליה אין מושיבין חנווני למחצית שכר וכל שכן הכא שקבל כל האחריות עליו נקט ליה משום סיפא מקבלין צאן ברזל מן העובד כוכבים עכ"ל וסיפא אתא לאשמועינן היתר רבית מן העובד כוכבים כדקתני לווין מהם ומלוין להן ברבית וקשה לפ"ה מאי פריך הכא ואי ס"ד ברשותא דמרא קיימא אמאי הוי רבית ברשותא דמרי קמשבח מאי קשיא מ"מ רבית דרבנן היא דכיון שכל אחריות על המקבל מלוה היא ונוטל חצי השבח בשכר המלוה אלא דלא הוי רבית דאורייתא כיון דאם לא יבא השבח לא יטול כלום כמו בלא נכייתא שהיא רבית דרבנן ונראה כמו שפי' ר"ת שהיא רבית דאורייתא שפסק דמים על הצאן ופסק דמי השבח וקבל עליו לתת בכל שנה ושנה בין יהא שם שבח בין לא יהיה ורבית גמורה היא דהיינו רבית קצוצה ויש לומר דהכא תניא ואע"ג דתנא רישא היינו דחנווני שהוא רבית דרבנן והכא קמ"ל דההיא רבית דאורייתא היא כדקתני מפני שהוא רבית כלומר רבית דאורייתא ומיהו אשכחן מפני שהוא רבית דרבנן דתנן בב"מ (דף סד:) המלוה את חברו לא ידור בחצרו חנם ולא ישכור ממנו בפחות מפני שהוא רבית דפר"ת דלא איירי במשכנתא מדלא קתני המלוה על חצרו ועוד דשרי להשכיר בפחות כמו שדה וכרם דשרו בנכייתא משום דזימנין ליכא שבחא כלל ובית נמי זימנין דאיכא תיוהא שנופל או נשרף ופר"ת שהלוהו הלואה גמורה ולא על חצרו ואין זה רבית דאורייתא ולא בתורת רבית משאיל ומשכיר לו בפחות ומוחל ולפ"ה נמי נהי דלא ידור בחצרו חנם הוי רבית דאורייתא כמו בתי חומה דהוי רבית דאורייתא מה שמשכיר בפחות מיהא מסתבר דלא הוי דאורייתא ומיהו האי מפני שהוא רבית דהכא דאורייתא קאמר דאי לאו הכי מאי קמ"ל וכפי' ר"ת משמע בירושלמי דקאמר איזהו צאן ברזל היו לו ק' צאן אומר לו הרי הן עשויות עליך בק' דינרין של זהב ולדות חלב וגיזות שלך ואם מתו חייב אתה באחריותן ואתה מעלה לי סלע בכל אחת ואחת משלך באחרונה אסור משמע בהדיא ששם עליו השבח והקרן ואי לא מתני' דרבית לא הוה קשה ליה מתני' דהכא אמאי פטורין מן הבכורה דשפיר חשיבי ברשות עובד כוכבים כיון דאי לא יהיב זוזי תפיס לבהמה ואם לא משכח בהמה תפיס ולד שהכל משועבד לו מחמת קרן אבל למאי דחשבינן רבית דאורייתא קשה דא"כ יצא מרשות בעלים לגמרי כשאר מלוה ורבא מסיק דהא דפטורה מן הבכורה לא משום דקיימא לה ברשות מרה אלא משום דחשיב יד עובד כוכבים באמצע מכח שעבוד שיש לו כדמפרש ואזיל וא"ת מאי שנא מבהמת ארנונא דחייבת בבכורה ללישנא קמא דרבא פ"ק דפסחים (דף ו.) היכא דמצי ישראל לסלוקיה בזוזי והכא נמי אי יהיב ליה זוזי לא תפיס לולד וי"ל התם עיקר בהמה של ישראל מתחלה אלא שמשועבדת היא לארנונא וכיון דאפשר לסלוקיה בזוזי לא יצאה מרשות ישראל ולא חשיב יד עובד כוכבים באמצע אבל הכא דמתחלה של עובד כוכבים כ"ז שיש לעובד כוכבים כח זה דאי לא יהיב זוזי תפיס לבהמה לא יצאה מרשות עובד כוכבים ומקרי יד עובד כוכבים באמצע שלא נסתלקה ידו לגמרי:
notes.en: In brief: One may not accept tzon barzel from a Jew because it is interest (Bava Metzia 70b). Rashi there explained: interest, since he valued them for him in money, and as long as he has not paid his money they split the profit; and although the mishna seems superfluous, since it already taught that one may not set up a shopkeeper for half the profit (all the more so here, where he took all the liability), it is stated for the sake of the latter clause, that one may accept tzon barzel from gentiles, teaching that interest from gentiles is permitted. Difficulty for Rashi: what does our Gemara ask, “if it stood in the owner’s possession, why is it interest”? Even so it would be rabbinic interest: with all the liability on the recipient it is a loan and the owner takes half the gain for the loan, and it is not Torah interest only because if there is no gain he takes nothing. Rather, as Rabbeinu Tam explained, it is Torah interest: he fixed a price for the flock and a price for the gain and undertook to pay every year whether there is gain or not, which is fixed interest; and this mishna teaches that it is Torah interest, beyond the shopkeeper case, which is rabbinic. (Tosafot discusses here Bava Metzia 64b, “one who lends to his fellow may not live in his courtyard for free … because it is interest,” which Rabbeinu Tam explains as rabbinic; but here “because it is interest” must mean Torah interest, or what would it teach?) The Yerushalmi supports Rabbeinu Tam: “What is tzon barzel? He had a hundred sheep and said: they are charged to you at a hundred gold dinars; the offspring, milk and wool are yours; if they die you are responsible; and you pay me a sela for each one from your own” — the last is forbidden, clearly fixing both principal and gain. Without the interest mishna, our mishna would pose no difficulty: the animals would rightly count as in the gentile’s possession, since if unpaid he seizes the animal, or else the offspring, all being pledged to him for the principal. But once it is Torah interest, it has left the owner’s possession entirely like any loan; so Rava concludes that the exemption is not because it is in the owner’s possession but because the hand of a gentile is in the middle through his lien. If you ask: how is this different from an animal held for the arnona tax, which is obligated in the firstborn according to the first version of Rava in Pesaḥim (6a), where the Jew can pay off [the official] with money; here too, if he pays, the gentile does not seize the offspring? Answer: there the animal belonged to the Jew from the start and is only pledged for the arnona, and since he can pay it off it has not left his possession, so it is not “a gentile’s hand in the middle.” Here it belonged to the gentile from the start, and as long as he keeps the power to seize the animal if unpaid, it has not left his possession and is called “a gentile’s hand in the middle,” since his hand has not been entirely removed. notes.he: באותו תנאי שפירשתי למעלה:
notes.en: One may not accept tzon barzel from a Jew: on the same terms I explained above.

notes.he: דכיון דמקבל עליו כל האחריו' של בהמה מה שנותן לה חצי הולדות זהו רבית. ט"א דכיון דשם האמהות בדמים ונותן לו חצי הולדות הרי זה רבית דמשמע דמשום הכי נותנן לו שממתין לו מן הדמים:
notes.en: Because it is interest: since he takes upon himself all the liability for the animal, what he gives the owner, half the offspring, is interest. Another version: since he valued the mothers at a price and gives him half the offspring, this is interest, for it implies that he gives them to him for waiting for the money.

messages.text: Evidently, the investment stands in the possession of the recipient, as otherwise it would not be considered a loan.

notes.he: דמקבל זוזי הוא דאיחייב להו והאי דשקיל נותן חצי ולדות בשכר המתנת מעות קא שקיל להו דאי ברשות מרה קיימי אמאי רבית הוא ברשותא דמריה אשבח ולדות:
notes.en: Stands in the recipient’s possession: for it is the recipient who is obligated for the money, and what the giver takes, half the offspring, he takes as payment for waiting for the money. For if the animals stood in the owner’s possession, why would it be interest? The offspring grew in their owner’s possession.

notes.he: הבהמה דאי ברשותא דנותן קיימא הא ילדה ברשותו ולא הוי רבית:
notes.en: Evidently it stands in the possession of the recipient: the animal; for if it stood in the giver’s possession, it gave birth in his possession and it would not be interest.

messages.text: This is not difficult. This case, i.e., the mishna here, is where the gentile owner of the sheep accepts upon himself the responsibility for losses due to an accident or depreciation in the market value, and that is why the sheep are considered to still belong to him.

notes.he: העובד כוכבים אונסא וזולא:
notes.en: [Our] mishna: is where the gentile took upon himself accident and depreciation.

notes.he: מתני' להכי קיימא ברשותיה דעובד כוכבים ופטורה מן הבכורה דקביל עליה עובד כוכבים [אונסא] וזולא דבהמה:
notes.en: It is not difficult: our mishna stands in the gentile’s possession, and so is exempt from the firstborn, for this reason: that the gentile took upon himself accident and depreciation of the animal.

messages.text: And that case, the mishna in Bava Metzia, is where the owner did not accept upon himself responsibility for losses due to an accident or depreciation. Therefore, the guaranteed investment stands in the possession of the recipient.

notes.he: והכא גבי ישראל דקביל עליה המקבל אונסא וזולא הילכך הוי רבית:
notes.en: And here, regarding a Jew, the recipient took upon himself accident and depreciation; therefore it is interest.

messages.text: @Abaye If the owner accepted upon himself responsibility for losses due to an accident or depreciation, can you call it a guaranteed investment? This case is not a guaranteed investment, as the owner is not guaranteed to receive what he had given; rather, it is a type of joint business venture that is permitted between two Jews.
messages.quote: accepts upon himself the responsibility for losses due to an accident or depreciation

notes.dh: אי דקביל עליה אונסא וזולא צאן ברזל קרית ליה
notes.he: בתמיה הא צאן ברזל לא הוי אלא במקבל עליה המקבל אונסא דלהכי קרית ליה ברזל קשה ואינו נפחת כך זה הנותן לא יפחות מדמיו:
notes.en: If he took upon himself accident and depreciation, do you call it tzon barzel? Asked in astonishment: tzon barzel is only where the recipient takes the accident upon himself, for that is why you call it “iron”: it is hard and does not diminish; so too for the giver, he will receive no less than its value.

messages.text: And furthermore, if the term: Guaranteed investment, can refer to two different kinds of investments, then why was it stated without qualification in both mishnayot?

notes.he: בתמיה. כלומר פסקה למילתא דיש חילוק בין צאן ברזל לצאן ברזל:
notes.en: And furthermore, why the unqualified statement? Asked in astonishment: that is, it states the matter without qualification, although there is a distinction between one tzon barzel and another.

messages.text: And furthermore, even if one grants that this arrangement can be called a guaranteed investment, there is another difficulty. Instead of the tanna teaching in the latter clause of the mishna in Bava Metzia: But one may accept a guaranteed investment from gentiles, let the tanna distinguish and teach within the case itself, that of accepting a guaranteed investment from a Jew.

notes.he: דהתם אבל מקבלין כו':
notes.en: Instead of teaching the latter clause: there [in Bava Metzia], “but one may accept, etc.”

messages.text: He should have taught: In what case is this statement, i.e., that one may not accept from a Jew sheep to raise or other items to care for as a guaranteed investment, said? It is in a case when the owner did not accept upon himself responsibility for losses due to an accident or depreciation, but if the owner accepted upon himself responsibility for losses due to an accident or depreciation, one may well enter into such an arrangement.

notes.he: במקבל מישראל דפעמים מקבלין ופעמים אין מקבלין בד"א וכו'. ואמאי אצטריך למיתנא אבל מקבלין מן העובד כוכבים אפילו מישראל נמי:
notes.en: Let it distinguish within it: in the case of one who receives from a Jew, that sometimes one may accept and sometimes one may not: “In what case is this said, etc.” And why did it need to teach “but one may accept from a gentile”? Even from a Jew [one may, in such a case].

messages.text: Both this case in the mishna here and that case in Bava Metzia are discussing a situation where the owner did not accept upon himself responsibility for losses due to an accident or depreciation.

notes.he: הא והא דלא קביל עליה מרא אונסא וזולא אלא על המקבל יהא הכל:
notes.en: Rather: both this and that are where the owner did not take accident and depreciation upon himself, but everything is on the recipient.

notes.he: בין מתניתין דבכורות בין מתני' דבבות דלא קביל עליה הנותן:
notes.en: Both this and that: both the mishna in Bekhorot and the mishna in Bava [Metzia] are where the giver did not take it upon himself.

messages.text: And here, with regard to the firstborn, this is the reason that the offspring are exempt from the halakhot of a firstborn: Since, if the gentile comes and wants his money, and the Jew does not give it to him, the gentile will seize the animal, and if he does not find the animal he will seize the offspring, this means that the hand of a gentile is in the middle, i.e., even though the animals stand in the possession of the recipient, the gentile has some degree of ownership over the bodies of the offspring.

notes.he: לאו משום דהוי ברשותו של עובד כוכבים אלא משום דמשכון הוי גביה:
notes.en: And here, regarding the firstborn: it is not because it is in the gentile’s possession, but because it is held as a pledge for him.

notes.he: מ"ט פטורה מן הבכורה דאילו אתי עובד כוכבים כו':
notes.en: And here: what is the reason it is exempt from the firstborn? Because if the gentile comes, etc.

messages.text: And there is a halakha: In every case where the hand of a gentile is in the middle, the animal is exempt from the halakhot of a firstborn.

§ The mishna teaches: If the Jew established their offspring in place of their mothers for collection in case the mothers die, the offspring of their direct offspring are exempt. The Gemara cites a dispute with regard to animals involved in a guaranteed investment, in a case where the Jew did not establish their offspring in the place of their mothers.
messages.quote: established their offspring in place of their mothers

messages.text: Their direct offspring are exempt, but the offspring of their direct offspring are obligated.

notes.dh: אמר רב הונא וולדן של צאן ברזל פטורים כו'
notes.he: כדפריש' גבי מתני' וארישא קאי:
notes.en: Rav Huna said: the offspring of tzon barzel are exempt, etc.: as I explained on the mishna; and this refers to the first clause.

notes.he: רב הונא ורב יהודה ארישא דמתניתין פליגי המקבל צאן ברזל מן העובד כוכבים:
notes.en: Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda disagree about the first clause of the mishna, “one who receives tzon barzel from a gentile.”

messages.text: The offspring of their direct offspring are also exempt, and the offspring of the offspring of their direct offspring are obligated.

notes.dh: רב יהודה אמר ולדי ולדות נמי פטורין
notes.he: ודור ד' לצאן ברזל אינו נותן לכהן אלא דור ה'. ולקמן פריך ליה ממתני':
notes.en: Rav Yehuda says: the offspring of offspring are also exempt: and the fourth generation of the tzon barzel he does not give to the priest, only the fifth. And below [17a] the Gemara raises a difficulty against him from the mishna.

notes.he: וולדי ולדות נמי פטורין דקא דייק בלישנא דמתניתין באותו ענין מה שנקדתי בדף כעין מחק בפירוש המשנה:
notes.en: The offspring of offspring are also exempt: for he infers this from the wording of the mishna in that matter, as I marked with dots on the page, like an erasure, in the explanation of the mishna.

messages.caption: Which generations of a flock taken from a gentile as tzon barzel are exempt from the firstborn, according to the mishna, Rav Huna, Rav Yehuda and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

messages.text: The Gemara raises an objection to the opinion of Rav Yehuda. We learned in the mishna: If the Jew established their offspring in place of their mothers for collection in case the mothers die, the offspring of their direct offspring are exempt.
messages.quote: The offspring of their direct offspring are also exempt

messages.text: The reason they are exempt is that he established the offspring in place of their mothers; but if he did not establish them in place of their mothers, they are not exempt. This is apparently a conclusive refutation of the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda.

notes.he: שהחזיק כחו של עובד כוכבים הא לא העמיד לא מיפטרי ולדי ולדות של צאן ברזל:
notes.en: The reason is that he established: that he strengthened the gentile’s claim; but if he did not establish, the offspring of the offspring of the tzon barzel are not exempt.

notes.dh: טעמא דהעמיד הא לא העמיד לא תיובתא דרב יהודה
notes.he: תימה דלקמן פריך לרב יהודה ממתני' דקתני בהדיא המקבל צאן ברזל מן העובד כוכבים ולדות פטורין מן הבכורה וולדי ולדות חייבין ומשני אימא הן וולדותיהן פטורין פירוש הן הולדות של צאן ברזל וולדותיהן הן וולדי ולדות פטורין מליתן בנם לכהן שהוא רביעי דצאן ברזל ואף על גב דלא קתני הן במתניתין צריך לומר דפשיטא ליה דולדות של צאן ברזל הן כצאן ברזל עצמן ולא אצטריך ליה במתניתין תו למיתני ואם כן גם כאן אמאי לא מפרש כן דכשמתו האמהות והעמיד הולדות תחת אמותיהן נעשו הולדות עצמן צאן ברזל וכי קתני ולדי ולדות פטורין היינו ולד ולדי ולדות שנפרש הן היינו ולדי ולדות וולדותיהן (פטורין) [היינו ולד ולדי ולדותיהן פטורין] הא לא העמיד חייבין וי"ל דלכך פי' בקונטרס במתני' העמיד לאו ממש שמתו האמהות והעמיד הולדות תחתיהן אלא שפתח לו פתח לעובד כוכבים שאם ימותו האמהות יהיו ולדות תחתיהן ועוד יש לומר דאפילו איירי במתו כדמשמע בתוספתא אין זה העמדה גמורה שלא עשה לו שום קנין בולדות אלא הסמיכו עליהן בדיבור בעלמא:
notes.en: In brief: The reason is that he established, but if he did not establish, no: a refutation of Rav Yehuda. It is puzzling: below [17a] the Gemara challenges Rav Yehuda from the mishna’s explicit words, “the offspring are exempt and the offspring of offspring are obligated,” and answers: read “they and their offspring are exempt,” meaning that the offspring of the tzon barzel are like the tzon barzel themselves, and their offspring, the offspring of offspring, are exempt from giving their young, the fourth generation, to the priest; and though the mishna does not say “they,” it must be obvious to the Gemara that the offspring of tzon barzel are like the tzon barzel themselves. If so, why not explain here too that when the mothers died and he established the offspring in their place, the offspring themselves became tzon barzel, so that “the offspring of offspring are exempt” means one generation further, while without establishing that generation is obligated [and Rav Yehuda would not be refuted]? Answer: that is why Rashi explained in the mishna that “established” does not literally mean that the mothers died and he set the offspring in their place, but that he opened a door for the gentile that if the mothers die the offspring will stand in their place. Alternatively, even if it speaks of where they died, as the Tosefta implies, this is not a full establishing, since he made no act of acquisition in the offspring but merely relied on them for him by word alone. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: כשהעמיד מוסיף דור אחר לפטור אבל לא העמיד אין מוסיף דור אחר:
notes.en: If he established, yes: when he established, he adds another generation to the exemption; but if he did not establish, he does not add another generation.

messages.text: The Aramaic here reads Rav Yehuda (רב יהודה), the Amora of the dispute above, whom the translation calls “Rabbi Yehuda” in this line.

Rav Yehuda could have said to you: That inference is incorrect, as the same is true even though he did not establish the offspring in place of their mothers. In that case as well, the offspring of their offspring are exempt. And this is what the mishna is teaching us by stating the halakha in that manner: Even if he established the offspring in place of the mother, only the first two generations of offspring are exempt, but not all successive generations.

notes.he: דאע"ג דהעמיד דאורחיה דעובד כוכבים למיזל ולמיתפס בנה כלומר סד"א כיון שחוזר כח עובד כוכבים בולדות אימא יהיו פטורין לעולם קמ"ל אפילו הכי ולדות של אותן ולדות שהן ולדי ולדות לצאן ברזל פטורין וולדי ולדות של ולדות חייבין כאילו לא העמיד:
notes.en: And this teaches us: that although he established, since it is the gentile’s way to go and seize her young. That is, you might have thought that since the gentile’s claim returns onto the offspring, they should be exempt forever; it teaches us that even so, the offspring of those offspring, which are the offspring of the offspring of the tzon barzel, are exempt, and the offspring of the offspring of the offspring are obligated, as though he had not established.

notes.dh: א"ל הוא הדין דאף על גב דלא העמיד
notes.he: ולדי ולדות פטור כדאמינא. והאי דקתני העמיד רבותא קמ"ל דאע"ג דהעמיד דיהב ליה אפותיקי אפילו הכי אי לא משכח ההיא דהעמיד תפיס ליה בנה דהיינו ולדי ולדות הילכך פטירי שאחריות לעובד כוכבים כלומר דתפיס אפילו דור עשירי תחותיה:
notes.en: He said to him: the same is true even though he did not establish; the offspring of offspring are exempt, as I said. And when it teaches “established,” it teaches us a novelty: that although he established, giving him a designated pledge [apotiki], even so, if he does not find the one he established, he seizes her young, that is, the offspring of offspring; therefore they are exempt, since their liability is to the gentile, that is, he seizes even the tenth generation in its place.

messages.text: And it is necessary to teach this halakha that although he established the offspring in place of their mothers all successive generations are not exempt, as one might think that it is the normal manner of the gentile to seize not only the direct offspring, but her young of any generation as payment, which would mean that all successive generations are exempt.

And therefore the mishna teaches that he is like one who did not establish the offspring in place of the mother, which means that the offspring of the direct offspring are exempt, but the offspring of the offspring of the direct offspring are obligated.

The Gemara raises an objection to the opinion of Rav Huna. We learned in the mishna that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: Even until ten generations the offspring are exempt, as they serve as a guarantee for the gentile, because if he does not receive the fixed payment for the animal he will collect his debt from any offspring born to it or its offspring.
messages.quote: Even until ten generations, the offspring are exempt, as they all serve as a guarantee for the gentile

notes.he: וקס"ד דר"ג ארישא קאי:
notes.en: We learned: Rabban Gamliel says, etc. [Rashi’s text reads Rabban Gamliel]: and it now enters our mind that he refers to the first clause.

messages.text: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel’s use of the term: Even, indicates that he disagrees with the first tanna only with regard to how many generations of offspring are exempt, but both agree that at least some generations are exempt. Granted, according to Rav Yehuda, who says that, in exempting from firstborn status, the first tanna descended to two generational levels…

notes.dh: בשלמא לרב יהודה דאמר נחית ת"ק
notes.he: למיפטר דרי דשתי דורות לצאן ברזל פוטר ת"ק:
notes.en: Granted according to Rav Yehuda, who says the first tanna descended: to exempting generations, for the first tanna exempts two generations of the tzon barzel.

notes.dh: בשלמא לרב יהודה דאמר דנחית תנא קמא לדרי
notes.he: ששני דורות פוטר ושלישי מחייב אמטו הכי נקט רשב"ג נמי לשון רוב דורות:
notes.en: Granted according to Rav Yehuda, who says the first tanna descended to generations: that he exempts two generations and obligates the third; for that reason Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel too uses the language of many generations.

messages.text: Continued on 17a: that is why Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says “even until ten generations”; but according to Rav Huna, the Gemara asks, what does “even” mean?
